name: Hairline-preserving cycle (DHT-conscious)

card.summary: A planning approach in physique culture of choosing compounds and add-ons thought to carry lower hair-loss risk, to protect the hairline while building muscle.
card.note: Involves performance drugs; androgens can accelerate hair loss in genetically predisposed people.

quick.overview:
People in physique forums who worry about male pattern baldness discuss choosing anabolic agents they consider less likely to worsen hair loss, and pairing them with DHT-lowering medications. The goal is to keep the hairline while pursuing muscle.

The discussion is community-driven and anecdotal: forum posts compare experiences, and no clinical trial of the strategy has been identified.
quick.how: In general terms, forum users compare which compounds they think are "hair-safe" and discuss add-ons such as finasteride. Details vary and are not reproduced here.
quick.risks: Anabolic steroid use carries wide-ranging documented health risks beyond hair loss, and DHT-lowering drugs have their own side effects. These are prescription or controlled substances in many countries; discussion with a physician is the standard guidance.

lead: The hairline-preserving, or "hair-safe", cycle is a concept in bodybuilding forums in which users select performance-enhancing compounds and add-ons they believe are less likely to trigger androgenetic hair loss. Appearance-wise, the aim is to build muscle without losing hair.

The idea rests on the belief that conversion of androgens to dihydrotestosterone (DHT) contributes to male pattern baldness in predisposed people. Forum threads on T Nation ask, for example, whether a given compound is "the most hair-safe" for someone prone to hair loss [1].

Users report mixed experiences: some say they have kept thick hair through years of androgen use, others describe stopping testosterone therapy because of hair loss [2][3]. No clinical study has tested hair-safe protocols.

chain: Select compounds and add-ons believed to lower DHT-related risk
Lower chance of hairline recession (as claimed)
angle.text: Users pursue this to retain hair while training with androgens. The claimed effect is reduced hairline recession.

infobox: Compounds vary; many are controlled or Rx-only

paras: The concept concerns hair-loss risk management among people using androgens. Users ask which agents they consider gentler on hair [1].

A user of a first-cycle thread asks whether one compound is the safest for hair [1]. Another describes thick hair after years of TRT and blasts [2], and a separate thread discusses coming off TRT because of hair loss [3]. These are personal anecdotes.
No studies found. A registered trial under a similar name, "Hair-Safe Study", concerns scalp cooling for hair preservation in women undergoing chemotherapy and is unrelated [4].
